name: Ptosis surgery (levator advancement)

card.summary: Surgery to raise a drooping upper lid, mainly a functional operation whose appearance benefit (a more open eye) is discussed on forums; supported in medical series.
card.note: Not purely cosmetic in origin; revision surgery and lid asymmetry are possible.

quick.overview:
Ptosis surgery lifts an upper eyelid that sits too low. Levator advancement tightens or reattaches the levator aponeurosis, the tendon that lifts the lid, and is a standard approach for aponeurotic (age- or stretch-related) ptosis.

Beyond vision, looksmaxxing users discuss it for a more open, alert-looking eye. One looksmax.org member shared a before-and-after account of a bilateral repair.
quick.mechanism: Surgeons choose among levator advancement or resection, Muller muscle-conjunctival resection and frontalis sling depending on cause and levator function.
quick.risks: Wikipedia lists uneven lids, dry eye, bleeding, infection and rarely loss of lid movement; one study cited there found about half of surgical patients needed more surgery within 8 to 10 years.

lead: Ptosis surgery corrects drooping of the upper eyelid (blepharoptosis). Levator advancement, also called aponeurotic ptosis surgery, repairs the levator aponeurosis that has stretched or detached from the tarsal plate, and was described in the ophthalmic literature in 1979 with emphasis on preserving normal anatomy.[2]

Ptosis may be minimal (1-2 mm), moderate (3-4 mm) or severe (over 4 mm), and may be congenital or acquired with myogenic, neurogenic, aponeurotic, mechanical or traumatic causes.[1] Alternatives include Muller's muscle-conjunctival resection for mild ptosis with good levator function,[3][4] and fascia lata for severe cases.[5]

Evidence consists of case series, anatomy studies and functional-outcome studies, including one that linked vision-related impairment to surgery impact.[10] Looksmaxxing forums discuss ptosis repair as a way to open the eye.

paras: Classification covers myogenic, neurogenic, aponeurotic, mechanical and traumatic causes, and ptosis is usually isolated but can accompany systemic disorders.[1] Marginal reflex distance (MRD) is used to measure severity; Grokipedia gives a normal MRD1 of 4-5 mm.[11] Anatomical studies of the levator palpebrae superioris and orbital septum inform surgical planning.[6][7]

Aponeurotic surgery was presented as a revival of approaches that preserve tear-producing structures, Muller's muscle and Whitnall's ligament.[2] Muller's muscle-conjunctival resection, with the phenylephrine test used to guide the amount resected, treats minimal to mild ptosis with good levator function,[3][4] and fascia lata harvesting has documented donor-site complications.[5] Paediatric ptosis has been reviewed over 10 years.[9]

Wikipedia lists uneven eyelids, dry eyes, bleeding, infection and rare loss of eyelid movement as risks, and cites a study in which about half of surgical patients needed further surgery within 8 to 10 years.[12]
Wikipedia notes ptosis crutch glasses, scleral contact lenses and, since 2020, FDA-approved 0.1% oxymetazoline ophthalmic solution for acquired blepharoptosis.[12]

A looksmax.org member posted a personal account of ptosis surgery under local anaesthetic with an oral sedative, describing marginal reflex distance, mild swelling, and a result in which the lids no longer covered the corneal light reflex; a reply described a large improvement.[13]

Studies include case series and algorithms for Muller's muscle-conjunctival resection,[3][4] a paediatric 10-year review,[9] and a study correlating vision-related functional impairment with the impact of surgery.[10] Registered trials include a completed 180-participant study of a modified levator tucking technique (NCT04883853),[14] and trials comparing approaches for involutional (NCT03373812)[15] and severe (NCT03916107)[16] ptosis.

timeline.event: FDA approves oxymetazoline 0.1% drops for acquired ptosis (per Wikipedia).[12]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, ptosis repair is discussed as a way to open the eye, with first-person surgical accounts.[13]

claims.claim: Ptosis repair gives a more open, more attractive eye.
claims.believers: A poster says the operation uncovered the light reflex that his lids had covered, and a replying member called it a 'big improvement'.[13]
claims.experts: Medical literature frames the operation as functional, and one study correlated vision-related impairment with surgical impact; no study of attractiveness outcomes was found.[10]
